summary: 1 Chronicles 20 (8 verses) continues the story of temple. Starting with 'At the time of the return of the year, at the time when kings go out, Joab led out the army and wasted the country of the children of Ammon, and came and besieg', it moves through themes of temple, Davidic hope and calls readers toward worship.
whyItMatters: This chapter matters because it shows temple lived out in retelling david to cyrus. For a first-time reader, it answers: who is God in this moment, what does he ask, and how do people respond.

keyVerses.text: At the time of the return of the year, at the time when kings go out, Joab led out the army and wasted the country of the children of Ammon, and came and besieged Rabbah. But David stayed at Jerusalem
Again there was war with the Philistines; and Elhanan the son of Jair killed Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the staff of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.
These were born to the giant in Gath; and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.

questions.question: What is happening in 1 Chronicles 20?
questions.answer: In 8 verses, this chapter 1 chronicles 20 (8 verses) continues the story of temple. starting with 'at the time of the return of the year, at the time when kings go out, joab led out the army and wasted the country of the children of ammon, and came and besieg', it moves through themes of temple, davidic hope and calls readers toward worship. The setting is retelling david to cyrus, written to post-exile community. Look for who speaks, who listens, and what changes by the end.

questions.question: Who wrote 1 Chronicles and why 20 matters in the bigger story?
questions.answer: Traditionally chronicler, addressed to post-exile community around ~400 bc. This chapter fits the book's purpose as chronicle with genealogy — its themes of temple, Davidic hope build on what came before.

questions.question: Are there any difficult words here?
questions.answer: Scan for names, places, or repeated abstract words like righteousness, covenant, or glory. The glossary below defines up to 3 that show up most. Ask: who is this person, what does this word mean in everyday terms?

questions.question: What does this chapter teach about God or people?
questions.answer: Through temple and Davidic hope, it shows God's character (faithful, just, merciful) and human tendency (need, failure, hope). Notice how verses move from problem to provision.

questions.question: Verse 1 is long — what is it saying in plain English?
questions.answer: The verse says: 'At the time of the return of the year, at the time when kings go out, Joab led out the army and wasted the country of the children of Ammon, and came and besieged Rabbah. But David...' In plain terms: it is making a key point about temple. Break it into two halves — what is described, and what is promised or commanded.

questions.question: How could this chapter apply today without forcing modern ideas onto it?
questions.answer: Ask: what was original audience supposed to do with this? Then ask: what similar situation exists today? For example, if chapter warns about idols, today that might be money or status; if it celebrates deliverance, where do people need deliverance today?
